stories.title: Update: Jamia hunger strike reaches 11th day as talks with administration have not ended standoff
stories.body: The Federal reported on Friday 23 October that the hunger strike at Jamia Millia Islamia, which began on Monday 12 October, was in its 11th day. Talks with the administration started on day 10 through a high-level committee under the Vice-Chancellor but have not ended the standoff. The university reportedly proposed restoring the students' union after two months, which students questioned because examinations would fall in that period. The students' demands include restoring the union, the Chief Proctor's resignation, and an assurance of no legal or administrative action against protesters. The report says some strikers have developed health complications.
stories.check: Single source for the talks and the two-month proposal (The Federal, 23 Oct). Earlier reports differed on whether the strike had ended; The Tribune (22 Oct) and The Federal both describe it as continuing. Confirm current status and the proposal with Jamia and the students. No update for Saturday 24 October was found.

stories.title: Jamia holds Swachhata lectures at distance education centre and foreign languages department
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia issued two press releases dated Friday 23 October on lectures under its cleanliness campaign. At the Centre for Distance and Online Education on Thursday 22 October, a deputy director from the National Commission for Scheduled Castes outlined five principles for tidier offices and discussed the NAMASTE scheme on sanitation work. On Wednesday 21 October, the Department of Foreign Languages held an awareness lecture at Ho Chi Minh Hall, where a psychology faculty member spoke on cleanliness and the NSS and NCC. Participants took a Swachhta pledge.
stories.check: Single source: Jamia press releases 6168 and 6169. Release pages show headlines only; details come from the English PDFs. Confirm with Jamia.

stories.title: Jamia teacher education department hosts colloquium on privatisation and teaching
stories.body: The Department of Teacher Training and Non-Formal Education at Jamia Millia Islamia held a colloquium talk on "Privatisation, Teaching and Teacher Education" on Thursday 22 October in the Multimedia Lab, Salamatullah Building, according to a press release dated Friday 23 October. The speaker was an associate professor from Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi. He argued that privatisation should be seen as a discourse, set of policies and route to technological solutions, not only growth of private schools, and raised concerns about teachers' labour, surveillance and data demands. A question-and-answer session followed.
stories.check: Single source: Jamia press release 6172 (English PDF). Confirm with Jamia.

stories.title: Jamia Urdu teachers' academy holds online lecture on e-waste management
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia's Academy of Professional Development of Urdu Medium Teachers held an online special lecture, "E-Waste Management: Challenges and Sustainable Solutions", on Friday 23 October at 10.45 am, with DDU Kaushal Kendra, according to a press release of the same date. Speakers cited about 62 million tonnes of e-waste generated worldwide in 2022, of which 22.3 per cent was formally collected and recycled. They called for stronger regulation, producer responsibility and safer recycling, and urged individuals to repair devices, avoid status-driven replacement and dispose of e-waste through proper channels.
stories.check: Single source: Jamia press release 6173 (English PDF). The figures are as stated by speakers in the release; they were not independently checked.

stories.title: Jamia dentistry faculty marks World Endodontics Day with composite restoration masterclass
stories.body: The Faculty of Dentistry at Jamia Millia Islamia hosted a guest lecture and live demonstration, "Crafting Composites for Functional Restoration", on Wednesday 14 October in the Library Hall, a press release dated Friday 23 October says. It marked World Endodontics Day and was organised with the Indian Academy of Aesthetic and Cosmetic Dentistry. The guest speaker covered bonding, dentin conditioning and layering methods on a model. The release says about 100 participants, mainly final-year students, interns and postgraduates, attended.
stories.check: Single source: Jamia press release 6170 (English PDF). The event predates the release by nine days. Confirm with Jamia.
